about: BACKLOG GM-314: the figure test set. Each request is a figure an engineer asks the geotech page for, on a made-up project. Its numbers are the sample calc packages' own (docs/examples/sample_packages.json, GM-328): 'row' names the package method whose params the request passes; 'replace' swaps in the inputs of a method probe (funhouse_agent/tests/method_probes.json, made-up values) where the sample table has none for the figure (liquefaction), or, without a probe, the request's own made-up inputs (the stress history, R02); 'patch' changes one input (a shape, a load). 'kind' is what the figure is; 'named' is false where neither the figure helper's worked examples (aec_agent_core/charts/figure_examples.py) nor the tool texts name that figure (the owner asked for those). 'tests' lists the checklist items the request is chosen to test; 'extra' the items the request itself says must be on the figure. 'elevation' is a made-up ground surface elevation given in the request (a profile then has elevation on its vertical axis); without one, depth with the figure saying so. 'numpy_note' marks a request whose calculation integrates with numpy's trapezoid rule (the host's numpy 1.26.4; see the Foundry section).

requests.ask: For a made-up bridge pier on a square spread footing, draw the ultimate and the allowable bearing resistance against footing width from 1.5 m to 4.5 m, everything else as given.
extra: The 3.0 m design width is marked, with its ultimate and allowable (factor of safety 3.0) bearing resistance written in kPa.

requests.ask: For a made-up embankment site on soft clay, the ground surface is at El. 30.0 m. Draw the stress history of the clay against elevation: the effective overburden pressure and the preconsolidation pressure. Three oedometer tests gave preconsolidation pressures of 72 kPa at El. 27.0 m, 85 kPa at El. 24.0 m and 104 kPa at El. 21.0 m; the design profile is the clay layers' sigma_p in the inputs.
extra: Each oedometer test's preconsolidation pressure is a point (a marker), not joined to the others by a line, and named as test data.
The design preconsolidation profile is a line, named on the figure as the design profile.
The effective overburden pressure is drawn and named, in kPa, with elevation (El. 30.0 m at the ground surface) on the vertical axis.

requests.ask: For a made-up sign foundation pile, the ground surface is at El. 20.0 m. Draw the pile's lateral deflection, bending moment and shear under the 100 kN head load, side by side on one vertical axis, with the pile drawn.
extra: Deflection in mm, bending moment in kN-m and shear in kN.
The maximum bending moment and its elevation are written on the figure.

requests.ask: For the same made-up pile, draw the p-y curves of the sand at depths of 1 m, 3 m and 6 m below the ground surface.
extra: Each curve is named with its depth on the curve itself, not only in a legend.
Soil resistance p in kN/m and deflection y in mm.

requests.ask: For a made-up road embankment over soft clay, draw the cross-section with the soil layers, the given slip circle and its factor of safety.
extra: The factor of safety is written on or beside the slip circle.
The layers are named as the inputs name them (fill, softclay).

requests.ask: For a made-up cut slope, draw the cross-section with the critical slip surface of the entry-exit search and the ten lowest surfaces found.
extra: The entry and exit ranges are marked on the ground surface.
The critical surface stands out from the others and its factor of safety is written on it.

requests.ask: For a made-up rectangular footing 1.8 m by 7.3 m, draw Schmertmann's strain influence factor and each layer's modulus Es against depth below the footing.
extra: The peak strain influence factor and its depth are written on the figure.
The figure says it uses depth because no elevations are given.

requests.ask: For the same made-up footing, draw the immediate settlement with Schmertmann's time factor against time from 0.1 to 50 years.
extra: Settlement increases downward and time is on a log scale.
The settlement at 0.1 years is written on the figure in mm.

requests.ask: For a made-up abutment on HP12x74 piles, the ground surface is at El. 30.0 m. Draw the nominal shaft, toe and total axial resistance against the elevation of the pile toe, with the soil layers beside it.
extra: The groundwater level is drawn and named.
The layers are named as the inputs name them (L1 loose silty sand, and so on).

requests.ask: For a made-up drilled shaft, draw the unit side resistance and the cumulative side resistance against depth, showing the cased zone.
extra: The cased zone (the top 3.0 m) is marked as carrying no side resistance.
Unit side resistance in kPa, cumulative side resistance in kN.

requests.ask: For made-up square concrete piles through soft clay under new fill, draw the axial load in the pile and the settlement of the soil and of the pile against depth, with the neutral plane.
extra: The neutral plane is drawn across both panels and its depth is written.
The drag force is written in kN.

requests.ask: For a made-up 7.8 m abutment wall, draw the wall with the static active and the Mononobe-Okabe seismic active pressures behind it.
extra: The static thrust and the seismic thrust are told apart and named as Mononobe-Okabe names them.
Each resultant is written in kN/m with the height it acts at.

requests.ask: For a made-up pump station site, the ground surface is at El. 5.0 m. Draw the factor of safety against liquefaction at the three SPT test depths, with the cyclic stress ratio and the cyclic resistance ratio.
extra: A factor of safety of 1.0 is drawn as a reference line and named.
Each test is a point; any line through the points is named as an assumed profile.

requests.ask: For a made-up cantilever retaining wall with backfill sloping at 10 degrees, draw the wall to scale with the active earth pressure on it and the bearing pressure under the base.
extra: The bearing pressure at the toe and at the heel is written in kPa.
The sloping backfill is drawn.

requests.patch_note: the spacings and 'no drains' are the request's own cases on the row's soil
requests.ask: For a made-up embankment on soft clay with prefabricated vertical drains, draw the average degree of consolidation against time for drains at 1.5 m, 2.4 m and 3.0 m triangular spacing, and without drains.
extra: The design time of 0.82 years is marked.
Each spacing's curve is named on the curve.

requests.ask: For the same made-up embankment, compare the time to reach 90 percent average consolidation for three cases: no drains, drains at 2.4 m in a square pattern, and drains at 2.4 m in a triangular pattern.
extra: Each case is one point on a case axis named as the request names it, not joined by a line.

requests.ask: For a made-up abutment on an 11 by 2 pile group, draw a plan of the pile cap with each pile's axial load under the given vertical load and moment. No plan of the site shows north.
extra: The pile cap outline is drawn and the most heavily loaded pile's load is written in kN.
The north arrow points straight up and the figure says no plan shows north.

requests.ask: For a made-up 4.6 m deep trench with a cantilever soldier pile wall, draw the wall with the net earth pressure on it and its bending moment beside it.
extra: The required embedment and the maximum bending moment are written on the figure.

requests.ask: For a made-up 10 m excavation with a two-level anchored wall, draw the wall with the apparent earth pressure envelope, the anchors at their levels and the anchor loads.
extra: Each anchor is drawn at its depth and inclination with its load written in kN/m or kN.

requests.ask: For a made-up retaining wall's sliding check, draw the probability distribution of the factor of safety and shade the probability that it is below 1.0.
extra: The probability of failure and the reliability index are written on the figure as the calculation gives them.

requests.ask: For a made-up county road, draw the designed flexible pavement section to scale: asphalt, granular base and granular subbase with their thicknesses.
extra: Each layer's thickness is written in mm and each layer is named as the design names it.

requests.ask: For a made-up 20 m clay column under a 100 kPa load, draw the excess pore pressure against depth at five of the given times.
extra: Each time's curve is named with its time on the curve.
Excess pore pressure in kPa, starting at zero.
